subject: FastShip performance discovery — load handoff & token velocity check
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@fastship.io>, Samir Patel <samir@fastship.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastShip performance discovery — load handoff & token velocity check

Hi Lucy / Samir —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size the pilot:

Summary from our call (please correct anything I missed):
- Steady-state QPS: ~110–130 qps (production baseline)
- Peak crest: up to ~2.7k qps for short bursts (30–90s) during marketing spikes
- Avg tokens per generation: 400 tokens (checkout confirmations + line-item summaries)
- Streaming mix: ~70–75% of requests use streaming (incremental order updates)
- Active concurrency at peak: ~600–700 concurrent streams/sessions
- Region: primary traffic in us-east-1; small eu footprint

SLOs you called out:
- 95th generation latency target: <350 ms
- 99th: acceptable up to ~800 ms during peaks, but prefer mitigation
- First-byte streaming requirement: <200 ms for interactive checkout flows

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you upload a 24–72 hour sample workload dump (CSV or json) with timestamps, request token counts, and streaming flag? — we referenced an example schema during the call; attach if you can.
2) Confirm whether the 2.7k qps peaks are single-region or multi-region bursts.
3) Any constraints around quantized models / acceptable quality delta if we suggest int8 quantization?

I've looped in Marissa (IO) to validate SLO mappings and Ben (capacity) to draft a lightweight sizing estimate. We'll aim to have an initial estimate and a short follow-up ops call (30–45m) on Wed 5/27 — does that work for you?

Attachments: please attach the workload snapshot (CSV) if available.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
[Attachment: call_recording_20260523.mp3 (audio)]

From: Lucy Chen <lucy@fastship.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@fastship.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastShip performance discovery — load handoff & token velocity check

Thanks Jordan — great recap. Couple clarifications and I've attached the workload snapshot you asked for.

Key clarifications:
- Peak bursts hit ~2,700 qps and lasted up to ~90s during our 2026-04 campaign; those are single-region (us-east-1).
- Steady-state baseline is closer to 115 qps.
- Average tokens per request is ~420; median is ~320 (skew from long receipts).
- Concurrency: peak active streaming sessions around 650.
- Streaming behavior: client-side keeps an open connection until confirmation; partial tokens are frequent.

SLO firming:
- We need 95th <350ms in normal operation; during marketing peaks we accept up to 900 ms p99 but want strategies to avoid wasted CPU.

Attachments:
- fastship_workload_snapshot.csv (CSV) — includes timestamp, tokens, streaming_flag, latency_sample

Questions for Redwood:
- If we use int8 quantized variants, what expected delta in summary quality should we assume?
- Will prefix caching help for repeated receipt templates?

We are available for Wed 5/27 10am PT. Thanks — Lucy

--
Lucy Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FastShip
lucy@fastship.io
[Attachment: fastship_workload_snapshot.csv (csv)]

Subject: Re: FastShip performance discovery — load handoff & token velocity check

Thanks Lucy — file received and very helpful. Loud and clear on the single-region bursts and the 420 avg tokens (median 320) — that's useful for batching heuristics.

Ben / Marissa — can you both take initial passes:
- Ben: rough capacity sketch for a pilot that meets 95th <350ms for steady-state and has a clear plan for dealing with 2.7k qps short crests (buffering / burst capacity). Please include a simple tokens/sec -> GPU slot mapping and an expected concurrency headroom number.
- Marissa: suggestion for warm-up (gradual traffic shift, prefix cache population) and recommended batching window to keep p95 latency under target while allowing aggregation for cost efficiency.

Lucy — Wed 5/27 10am PT works; I'll send a calendar invite for 30 minutes and we'll include an ops-runbook draft + a first-pass sizing.

Regards,
Jordan

Subject: FS sizing proposal (v1) — steady vs crest capacity and quick numbers

Jordan / team — attached is a short pilot sizing proposal (fs-sizing-proposal-v1.xlsx). Highlights below for discussion on Wed: 

Quick throughput math (based on Lucy's snapshot):
- Avg tokens / request: 420 tokens
- Steady-state QPS (baseline): 115 qps -> ~48,300 tokens/sec
- Peak crest QPS: 2,700 qps -> ~1,134,000 tokens/sec (burst, 30–90s)

Estimated token throughput per GPU (sizing assumptions; model = curated open LLM, mixed int8 batching):
- H100-class (aggressive batching): ~130k tokens/sec
- A100-80GB (conservative): ~60k tokens/sec

Initial pilot recommendation:
- Reserve 2 x A100-80GB for steady-state (combined sustained ~120k tokens/sec) -> comfortably covers baseline with headroom for p95 targets.
- Pre-warm 2 additional A100s as burst pool (autoscale to 4) to cover short crests; use rapid autoscale + short-lived burst buffer to meet peak token needs.
- If peaks > ~2x current crest in future, switch burst pool to H100 nodes or increase burst slots.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Use prefix caching for repeated receipt templates (expected to cut token work ~15–25% on common paths).
- Short batching window (5–12 ms) for streaming paths to preserve interactivity while allowing aggregation for cost wins.
- Canary ramp (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) over 10–15 min for warm-up; populate KV prefix cache proactively with recent templates.

Ballpark pilot cost and timeline:
- Pilot (reserved steady + burst autoscale) estimated 2–4 weeks to validate with traffic replay.
- Will share hourly cost estimates in the sizing workbook ahead of Wed meeting.

Next steps: I'll attach the spreadsheet now and Jordan will send the Wed invite (30 min). Marissa, please add warm-up checklist items to the shared doc.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
